Let me reconsider: We have 4 aromatic protons, so it's monosubstituted benzene (5H total) or disubstituted with symmetry (4H). The coupling patterns (ddd) suggest ortho, meta coupling, so likely monosubstituted or 1,2-disubstituted.

The two equivalent methyls at δ 2.69 (6H) could be N(CH₃)₂ or two OCOCH₃ groups.

Given carbonyl at 168.30 ppm (ester/amide), CH at 58.70 ppm (CH-O or CH-N), and the fact that we have CH₃-CH- pattern, maybe it's an ester of lactic acid derivative: CH₃-CH(OCOCH₃)-CO-N(CH₃)₂? Too complex.

Maybe the "CH₃" at δ 1.43 is actually CH₃ of ethyl group, and the quartet at δ 5.05 is CH of ethyl group coupled to CH₃.
